title: Grand marshals and the order of bands and clubs in a parade
summary: Rene explains the sergeant at arms, first and second grand marshals, and how bands and clubs line up.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, who has the gavel, the sergeant of arms?

Uh, which one did you call the caller on in the meeting? What they call him? Sergeant of arms? Yeah, that's the one that had the gavel with him. You'll notice him, you see he had the gavel on him. He had the gavel with him in a parade to him.
Well, sometimes in a parade you see two of them with Sashes. Are they both grand marshals?

Yeah, first and second grand marshal. You see, there's supposed to be a grand marshal, the marshal club, and the grand marshal that matched the band. The grand marshal that matched the band is supposed to be in the front. And the grand marshal that marched the club is supposed to be in the back. That's called the second grand marshal. That's the, that's the way they set up. Amen.
Well, you said back something about when you used to play in bands, sometimes there'd be two bands in the parade. Where would the second band be?

Right behind that first club. See, the first grand marshal in the band, then the club. Then another grand marshal, the band, and the other club. That's all they'd be sitting in the row team. And five, six, seven, eight clubs. You want the club behind that. Now, I don't know about the setting up, but I think the most prettiest club, I believe they set in the front. I believe. I don't know how that's raised, but I believe to my effect because the most of the ones in the front always did a beautiful, you know. Don't be much in the tail end, I noticed that. I guess we all know that same thing. But it's the same procedure, you know. One club behind the other. It's the same routine.
Well, what about when Black Benny died when he didn't belong to any clubs? Well, no, the same procedure.

There's a, there was the Zulu club, the Tannemith club, the Dewitt club, part of the Tulane club. In fact, putting every club in the city. Each one of them had their grand marshal. Each one, each club represented itself. See? And there were a lot of grocery men, a lot of borrow men, you know, corner bums and things. All they had their gang, see?
They were marching there, huh? Yeah. Out in the street. Not in the second line, but in the street.

Oh, they was in the street, yeah. Second line is the bank that marches. Sidewalk marches. And then sometimes it calls for, when they're going to make a stop somewhere, well, then the club get on the street. Get on the bank. Second line, get across the street. Or in the middle of the street. But mostly they get across the street, you know. So they're the second line, yeah.
